choice.combine: Skin cell with separated chromosome sets

reaction: The sequence clearly connects chromosome separation to the final split.

reaction: The final image of the person raising the arm gives the renewal processes a satisfying connection to the earlier body model.

mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the copied chromosomes and then dividing the skin cell made two distinct stages clear. The daughter cells then gave the skin-renewal construction a concrete purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the body was useful after the failed bone-cell combination, but the automatic skin-cell fitting made it feel more like a necessary transition than a meaningful choice.

surprise.text: I was interested that a low-oxygen cue at the kidney leads to a signal that helps red-cell precursors mature in marrow.

arbitrary.text: Combining the two bone-cell types seemed plausible from their descriptions, so the failure felt arbitrary at first. The later results clarified that removal and replacement occur in stages within the body.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it developed another relationship as clearly as the kidney-to-marrow signal. Much of this chapter's sequence was predictable, though the constructions helped connect cell activity to renewal in the whole body.
